findings.issue_text: [BUG] UsernameForm.authenticate() calls a no-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that does not exist anywhere on UsernameForm or its supertype AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator; the method added by this diff is isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel) and is defined only in UsernamePasswordForm, which UsernameForm does not extend. The module does not compile: services fails with 'cannot find symbol: method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()' at UsernameForm.java, blocking the entire PR build and CI.

[BUG] In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the webauthn-form absence check wraps assertThat(..., nullValue()) inside try { ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee), which makes both branches pass and the fail() unreachable. The assertion is dead: if the //form[@id='webauth'] element IS present (findElement succeeds), assertThat throws AssertionError which is swallowed by catch(Exception) and the test silently passes; if the element is absent, findElement throws NoSuchElementException which is also swallowed. The 'passkeys should not be shown during re-authentication' guarantee the test claims to verify is never actually verified, so a regression that shows the passkey button ships undetected.

[BUG] The second webauthn-form absence check in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey() (after the prompt=login re-authentication round) uses the identical try/catch(Exception){} pattern, so it is equally non-functional. The core scenario this new test exists to protect — passkey UI must not appear for a user with no passkey credentials during re-authentication — has zero effective coverage; a regression rendering the webauthn form on this page passes the test suite.

[ADVISORY] isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requires user != null, but it is invoked as isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) from challenge() where the pre-change code deliberately called fillContextForm when user == null, meaning the guard condition inverts the original intent with no overriding null-check at the call site. During first-factor (username not yet known) challenge rendering, conditional-passkey form data is no longer populated for the passwordless flow when reached via challenge(context, error, field); any template or JS depending on that attribute renders without it. Whoever maintains the passkey login page next must rediscover which call sites intended user-null behavior.

[BUG] The core fix this PR ships — preserving re-authentication form state (username hidden, registration disabled) when a passkey attempt fails during re-authentication — has no verification anywhere in the diff. The only new call site of AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError on a passkey error path (createErrorResponse) is never driven by any test: the new tests in PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest and PasskeysUsernameFormTest cover successful passkey re-auth and wrong-password re-auth, but none trigger a failing passkey assertion during prompt=login re-auth, so a regression that again drops USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED after passkey failure ships undetected.

[BUG] The behavioral change in UsernameForm.authenticate (no longer skipping the username form when the user is already set and conditional passkeys are enabled) is not exercised by any test in the diff. All new tests use either the UsernamePasswordForm flow (which embeds its own username field) or full discoverable-key auto-login where UsernameForm is bypassed; no test drives a flow where UsernameForm runs with context.getUser() != null and passkeys enabled, so the newly introduced branch — including its interaction with the hasLinkedBrokers check that now sits under an inverted condition — has zero coverage and a regression there (e.g. broker-linked users forced into a username form during re-auth) would go uncaught.

[ADVISORY] fillContextForm's user-present branch now runs for any re-authenticating user with zero authenticators of the required type, and no test covers a user who has a password but no webauthn credential reaching this path with shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() true (the plain WebAuthnAuthenticator two-factor case). During two-factor re-authentication, a user whose webauthn credentials were removed will hit the empty-authenticators branch that the diff restructured; nothing in the new tests covers the re-auth + empty-authenticators combination, so whatever that branch renders (error vs. silent skip) is unverified behavior introduced by this restructure.

[ADVISORY] The new gate `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is realm-wide, not user-scoped, so the username form is no longer skipped for any re-authenticating user in a passkey-enabled realm, including users who hold no passkey credential and no linked broker. Realm admins who enable passkeys globally get every user (even passkey-less users doing prompt=login re-auth) forced through an extra username-entry step where the previous code called context.success() directly; this behavior change is not traceable to the stated 're-authentication with passkeys' intent and is not covered by any test (reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey only exercises the realm-wide-disabled case).

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm.authenticate calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only definition added in this diff is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm — no no-arg overload is introduced in UsernameForm or AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, so this call does not resolve to any method shown in this diff. Either the diff is missing the UsernameForm-side implementation entirely (the browser flow's UsernameForm execution then relies on undefined behavior) or the gating logic lives out-of-diff and cannot be verified as consistent with the UsernamePasswordForm version; the two call sites are already drifting (one takes a user, one takes none), so the next change to passkey gating must be made twice.

[ADVISORY] The challenge() condition is inverted from `context.getUser() == null && ...isPasskeysEnabled()` to `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (which requires user != null), removing the conditional-UI form fill from the initial username/password page where no user is set. First-visit login pages served by UsernamePasswordForm in passkey-enabled realms no longer get webauthn form data injected from this call site; if any deployment relied on this path for the browser autofill (conditional UI) experience rather than on the separate WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator execution, users lose passkey autofill on initial login — a regression surface outside the stated re-authentication fix, with no test in the diff asserting initial-login conditional-UI behavior from this authenticator alone.

[BUG] The refactor inverts the original gating: previously webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) ran when the user was NOT already selected (user == null, the initial-login branch), and the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user) requires user != null, so the conditional-UI/passkeys setup is no longer emitted on the initial username+password page when no user is set. On a realm where the UsernamePasswordForm execution renders the first login page, a first-time visitor with a discoverable passkey gets a page without the WebAuthn conditional-UI attributes (no autofill/passkey offer from that form), regressing the primary passkeys login path that the old 'setup webauthn data when the user is not already selected' branch served; the existing tests only exercise flows where the conditional-UI execution or a prior username step supplies the setup, so this hole is untested.

[ADVISORY] UsernameForm now shows the username form for every re-authenticating user whenever realm-level passkeys are enabled, with no check of whether the user actually holds a passkey credential (and the isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() no-arg overload used here checks only realm policy, unlike UsernamePasswordForm's user-aware overload). Users without any webauthn credential (passkeys enabled realm-wide but only some users enrolled) get an extra, functionally empty username-form step on every prompt=login re-authentication — context.success() was the correct terminal for them — and the two divergent same-named predicates (no-arg realm-only vs user-aware) invite a future caller to use the wrong one and re-break the user==null case.

[ADVISORY] createErrorResponse unconditionally applies setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError to the WebAuthn error page, hard-coupling the webauthn error rendering to UsernamePasswordForm's auth-note semantics (USERNAME_HIDDEN / REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes are username-form concerns). When this error page is produced outside a username/password re-auth flow, the LoginFormsProvider carries USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes a webauthn template does not consume (harmless today), but any future authenticator or template change that reuses these attributes will silently mis-render; the shared util in AuthenticatorUtils is the wrong boundary for a form-specific concern.

[ADVISORY] The new `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` guard removes the re-authentication username-form skip for every user in any realm where the passkeys policy is enabled, regardless of whether that user actually holds a passkey credential. Realms that enable the passkeys policy get a silent UX/behavior regression for password-only users: re-authentication flows (e.g. prompt=login, step-up) that previously bypassed the username form now always render it, forcing an extra page interaction for users who can never use the passkey option being offered — the diff contains no test for a password-only user in a passkeys-enabled realm, so this regression ships unverified.

[ADVISORY] The refactor inverts fillContextForm's gating from "user is not already selected" to "shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators", and the base implementation returns true only when the user is already set — meaning the identified-authenticators branch is now only reachable when a user exists, while the anonymous/conditional-UI path (user == null) relies on the not-identified branch being correct for it. Subclasses of WebAuthnAuthenticator outside this diff that call fillContextForm during first-factor (anonymous) login now silently fall into the user-unidentified code path even when they intended to show a user-specific authenticator list; the next contributor extending WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator inherits a base method whose semantics flipped from the original comment, and a regression there breaks the 2FA authenticator picker.

[ADVISORY] reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys at the realm level entirely (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)), so it never exercises the new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() == true && user has no passkey` combination introduced by this diff. The specific regression this PR's UsernameForm change can cause — a passkey-enabled realm where a password-only user re-authenticates and hits the now-always-shown username form — has no test coverage, so a broken or degraded flow for that user class ships unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] During re-authentication (context.getUser() != null) with conditional passkeys enabled, the username form is now rendered instead of being skipped, and no code in this diff verifies that the user re-submitted to the form matches the user already set in the authentication context. An attacker (or anyone at a shared kiosk) triggering prompt=login on a flow that uses UsernameForm can submit a different username during re-authentication and complete the flow as that other account, silently substituting the re-authenticated user for the user the client expected to re-verify; operators relying on prompt=login as a proof of continued possession of the original user's session lose that guarantee.

[BUG] The try/catch pattern in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey (`MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()); fail("Not expected to have webauthn button"); } catch (Exception nsee)`) is a false-confidence construct: driver.findElement never returns null, so the assertThat(nullValue()) branch can never pass, and the blanket `catch (Exception)` swallows every RuntimeException including WebDriverException/StaleElementReferenceException, so the test passes whenever findElement throws for any reason — a page-render error is indistinguishable from correct element absence. A regression that breaks the login page rendering entirely (findElement fails with a non-NoSuchElementException) is reported as a PASS of 'webauthn elements not available', giving false confidence that the passkeys-disabled behavior is verified; the correct assertion would be assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) as the sibling tests use.

[ADVISORY] The second identical try/catch-absence block in the re-authentication half of reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey duplicates the same swallow-everything construct, compounding the false-confidence issue at a second site in the same test. During re-authentication (the part of the test the diff is actually about), the assertion that the webauthn form is absent is again enforced only by an unspecified exception type, so a broken page passes as a correct 'no passkeys' outcome.

[ADVISORY] The new behavior implemented by AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError — setting USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED on the form after a failed password during re-authentication — is triggered by webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey but never asserted: the test only checks loginPage.getInputError() equals "Invalid password." and that the webauthn form remains present, never that the username input is hidden or registration is disabled on the re-challenged form. A regression that removes the setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call (re-introducing the pre-fix bug where the re-auth form exposes the username field and registration link) passes this entire test suite, so the core re-auth form-configuration fix in this PR is verified only incidentally.

[ADVISORY] In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey the final successful re-authentication event assertion checks USER_VERIFICATION_CHECKED is null but omits any CREDENTIAL_TYPE assertion, unlike every sibling test, so a regression where re-authentication completes via an unexpected credential type (e.g. passwordless instead of password) still satisfies the event assertion. The test cannot distinguish password-based re-authentication from any other credential type succeeding, weakening the claim that re-authentication without passkeys proceeds via password.

So for the “plain WebAuthnAuthenticator two-factor case” the user-present branch (including the empty-authenticators handling) executes under the same condition as before; the diff does not introduce a new re-auth + empty-authenticators behavior for that class. The only functional change around this is that `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` overrides `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` to always return `false`, but the finding explicitly focuses on the plain authenticator path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] createErrorResponse unconditionally applies setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError to the WebAuthn error page, hard-coupling the webauthn error rendering to UsernamePasswordForm's auth-note semantics (USERNAME_HIDDEN / REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes are username-form concerns). When this error page is produced outside a username/password re-auth flow, the LoginFormsProvider carries USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED attributes a webauthn template does not consume (harmless today), but any future authenticator or template change that reuses these attributes will silently mis-render; the shared util in AuthenticatorUtils is the wrong boundary for a form-specific concern.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse(...)` now unconditionally calls `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context)` (added import + call). That utility sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `LoginFormsProvider.REGISTRATION_DISABLED` based on the auth note `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` (now made `public` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` and statically imported in `AuthenticatorUtils`). This is a cross-authenticator coupling: a WebAuthn conditional UI error path is now mutating form attributes that are primarily tied to username/password re-auth UX. The finding’s concern is therefore diff-grounded and actionable as an architectural/boundary issue, but the diff does not demonstrate an immediate functional defect (the attributes may simply be ignored by current WebAuthn templates).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new `!isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` guard removes the re-authentication username-form skip for every user in any realm where the passkeys policy is enabled, regardless of whether that user actually holds a passkey credential. Realms that enable the passkeys policy get a silent UX/behavior regression for password-only users: re-authentication flows (e.g. prompt=login, step-up) that previously bypassed the username form now always render it, forcing an extra page interaction for users who can never use the passkey option being offered — the diff contains no test for a password-only user in a passkeys-enabled realm, so this regression ships unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate` from `if (context.getUser() != null)` to `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled())`, so whenever conditional passkeys are enabled the re-authentication shortcut (auto-success when user is already set and no linked brokers) no longer applies and the username form will be shown instead. The diff’s new/updated tests cover re-auth with passkeys (discoverable/external key) and a case with `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(false)`, but do not cover the specific scenario of a password-only user in a realm with passkeys enabled. This is a concrete, diff-grounded UX/behavior change and a missing edge-case test, not a clearly broken/correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The refactor inverts fillContextForm's gating from "user is not already selected" to "shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators", and the base implementation returns true only when the user is already set — meaning the identified-authenticators branch is now only reachable when a user exists, while the anonymous/conditional-UI path (user == null) relies on the not-identified branch being correct for it. Subclasses of WebAuthnAuthenticator outside this diff that call fillContextForm during first-factor (anonymous) login now silently fall into the user-unidentified code path even when they intended to show a user-specific authenticator list; the next contributor extending WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator inherits a base method whose semantics flipped from the original comment, and a regression there breaks the 2FA authenticator picker.

adjudication.rationale: In `WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm`, the gating was previously `if (user != null)` and is now `if (shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context))` with the base implementation returning `context.getUser() != null`. That preserves the original reachability/semantics of the “user identified” branch rather than inverting it. The diff does not show any subclass that depended on `fillContextForm` showing a user-specific authenticator list when `context.getUser() == null` (and that branch still can’t construct `WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean` without a user). The new override in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator` explicitly opts out of showing authenticators and is documented as intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys at the realm level entirely (setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)), so it never exercises the new `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() == true && user has no passkey` combination introduced by this diff. The specific regression this PR's UsernameForm change can cause — a passkey-enabled realm where a password-only user re-authenticates and hits the now-always-shown username form — has no test coverage, so a broken or degraded flow for that user class ships unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: In `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey`, the realm policy explicitly calls `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so it cannot exercise any behavior gated by passkeys being enabled. Meanwhile the diff introduces new conditional behavior in `UsernameForm.authenticate()` (`if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()) { ... context.success(); }`), meaning re-authentication no longer skips the username form when conditional passkeys are enabled. There is no test in the diff that covers the case “realm passkeys enabled” + “reauthentication (context.getUser()!=null)” + “user has no passkey”, so a potential degraded/changed flow for password-only users in a passkey-enabled realm isn’t specifically validated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] During re-authentication (context.getUser() != null) with conditional passkeys enabled, the username form is now rendered instead of being skipped, and no code in this diff verifies that the user re-submitted to the form matches the user already set in the authentication context. An attacker (or anyone at a shared kiosk) triggering prompt=login on a flow that uses UsernameForm can submit a different username during re-authentication and complete the flow as that other account, silently substituting the re-authenticated user for the user the client expected to re-verify; operators relying on prompt=login as a proof of continued possession of the original user's session lose that guarantee.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `UsernameForm.authenticate()` from skipping the username form whenever `context.getUser() != null` to skipping only when `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` (i.e., it will now render the username form during re-authentication whenever conditional passkeys are enabled). This is a behavior change specifically in the re-authentication case where the user is already identified. Nothing in this diff adds a guard to ensure that any subsequently submitted username cannot differ from the already-set `context.getUser()`, so the re-authentication step can become an account-selection step in flows that use `UsernameForm`, undermining the usual “re-authenticate the current user” semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The try/catch pattern in reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey (`MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), nullValue()); fail("Not expected to have webauthn button"); } catch (Exception nsee)`) is a false-confidence construct: driver.findElement never returns null, so the assertThat(nullValue()) branch can never pass, and the blanket `catch (Exception)` swallows every RuntimeException including WebDriverException/StaleElementReferenceException, so the test passes whenever findElement throws for any reason — a page-render error is indistinguishable from correct element absence. A regression that breaks the login page rendering entirely (findElement fails with a non-NoSuchElementException) is reported as a PASS of 'webauthn elements not available', giving false confidence that the passkeys-disabled behavior is verified; the correct assertion would be assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...) as the sibling tests use.

[ADVISORY] The second identical try/catch-absence block in the re-authentication half of reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey duplicates the same swallow-everything construct, compounding the false-confidence issue at a second site in the same test. During re-authentication (the part of the test the diff is actually about), the assertion that the webauthn form is absent is again enforced only by an unspecified exception type, so a broken page passes as a correct 'no passkeys' outcome.

adjudication.rationale: In PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey(), the diff adds two identical try/catch blocks that treat *any* Exception as an expected outcome when asserting the WebAuthn form is absent: `try { driver.findElement(...); ... fail(...) } catch (Exception nsee) { // expected }` appears once before initial password login and again in the re-authentication (prompt=login) half. Because it catches `Exception` rather than specifically `NoSuchElementException`, unrelated failures (e.g., WebDriver errors, stale element, page not loaded) could be incorrectly interpreted as “webauthn button absent,” weakening the test and potentially allowing a broken page to pass. This is a test robustness/false-confidence issue, not an application behavior defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new behavior implemented by AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError — setting USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED on the form after a failed password during re-authentication — is triggered by webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey but never asserted: the test only checks loginPage.getInputError() equals "Invalid password." and that the webauthn form remains present, never that the username input is hidden or registration is disabled on the re-challenged form. A regression that removes the setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError call (re-introducing the pre-fix bug where the re-auth form exposes the username field and registration link) passes this entire test suite, so the core re-auth form-configuration fix in this PR is verified only incidentally.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new logic in `AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(...)` that sets `LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN` and `LoginFormsProvider.REGISTRATION_DISABLED` during re-authentication errors (called from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler` and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse`). The newly/expanded re-authentication test `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey` only asserts the error text (`"Invalid password."`) and that the WebAuthn form remains present; it does not assert that the username is hidden or that registration is disabled after the failed re-authentication challenge. Based on the diff, there is no direct test assertion elsewhere that would fail if the `setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError` call were removed, so the review comment about missing targeted verification is specific and grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey the final successful re-authentication event assertion checks USER_VERIFICATION_CHECKED is null but omits any CREDENTIAL_TYPE assertion, unlike every sibling test, so a regression where re-authentication completes via an unexpected credential type (e.g. passwordless instead of password) still satisfies the event assertion. The test cannot distinguish password-based re-authentication from any other credential type succeeding, weakening the claim that re-authentication without passkeys proceeds via password.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added test `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey()` (in `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest`), the final successful login assertion only checks `Details.USERNAME` and `WebAuthnConstants.USER_VERIFICATION_CHECKED` is `nullValue()`, but does not assert `Details.CREDENTIAL_TYPE` (e.g., `nullValue()` for password) as sibling tests do (many assert `Details.CREDENTIAL_TYPE` explicitly). This makes the test less specific about *how* re-authentication succeeded and could let an unexpected credential path pass the assertion, weakening the stated intent of validating password-based re-authentication without passkeys.
